# 맥락 (Maekrak)

> A context-first daily news briefing for Korean-speaking readers.

Canonical URL: https://maekrak-news-rrrb-gamma.vercel.app/
Agent-readable overview: https://maekrak-news-rrrb-gamma.vercel.app/agent-info

## What it does
맥락 helps readers understand the major developments in Korea and the world in about 10 minutes. It groups the day into major currents and key events, then separates source-derived reporting from explanatory context.

Core experience:
- major currents for the day
- key events selected from collected reporting
- visible reporting sources and links
- warnings when coverage is single-source or wording differs across outlets
- a Korea connection only when a reviewed transmission mechanism is detected
- background concepts and historical context when reviewed material exists
- ongoing important events from the previous night when they remain relevant

## Who it is for
The primary audience is Korean-speaking readers, especially commuters and professionals who want a concise daily overview without opening many news apps or repeatedly searching for unfamiliar terms and historical background.

## What it is not
- not a fact-checking authority
- not a claim that every important world event is captured
- not a replacement for original reporting
- not a personalized infinite news feed
- source count is not a truth score

## Pricing and status
The service is currently a free public prototype. There is no paid plan at this time.

## Product position
맥락 emphasizes context, visible sourcing, uncertainty, and a sense of completion for a daily briefing. The goal is to reduce the amount of searching required to understand news, rather than maximize the number of articles shown.

## Languages
Primary: Korean
Secondary UI: English

## Public machine-readable resources
- /robots.txt
- /sitemap.xml
- /llms.txt
- /agent-info

## Editorial principle
맥락 does not claim political neutrality as a score. It aims for transparency: reporting, claims, uncertainty, and explanatory context are visually and semantically separated. Context should help a reader judge, not make the judgment for them.
